transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is… it’s this thing that happens at night, mostly. I’ll start picking at leftovers in the kitchen, just a little here and there, and then it’s like the reasonable part of me is saying, “That’s enough, Alejandro, stop now,” but my hand keeps going back anyway.

It sounds silly when I say it out loud. I used to be pretty disciplined about other things—well, back when I was taking classes years ago, I could sit and study for hours if I had to—but with this, once I start, I don’t seem to steer it very well.

When you find yourself picking at food at night, does it feel like you’re eating large amounts of food in a short period, and do you feel like you can’t stop or control how much you eat during those times?

Yes… yes, that’s the part that bothers me. I mean, I don’t know how to measure “large,” exactly—my wife used to say I was always bad at judging portions, even back when we’d go to those cafeteria places where they give you a tray—but once I start with the leftovers late at night, it feels like I lose the steering wheel.

The sensible part of me is saying, “That’s enough, Alejandro, close the fridge,” but then my hand goes back for more anyway. It’s not like I’m sitting down planning some big meal. It just keeps going past where I meant it to stop.
Does this nighttime eating cause you distress or interfere with your daily life in any way?

It does bother me, yes. I mean, I’m not missing appointments or anything like that—I still get to the store, pay the bills, help around the house, all those regular things. I’ve always been pretty particular about keeping my little list for errands, actually, with the boxes to check off… though sometimes I forget the list on the kitchen table, which defeats the purpose.

But the mornings after it happens, I feel kind of heavy and sluggish, like I’m starting the day already disappointed in myself. Not so much that everything falls apart, but enough that I think, “Alejandro, you’re not handling this the way you should.”
After these nighttime eating episodes, do you ever try to make up for it by doing something like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising more than usual?

I don’t… I don’t think I really do anything like that, no. I mean, after it happens I mostly just feel bad and try to get on with the morning.

Exercise more than usual—well, “more than usual” is funny, because my usual is mostly walking around the neighborhood or to the store if the weather’s decent. I used to be better about walking when I had a regular route, before they changed the bus stop near us and I got out of the habit. But I’m not, you know, doing something extreme afterward.

And the other things you mentioned… no, I haven’t been making myself sick or anything like that.
